title: Pumpkin risotto
intro: The pumpkin melts into the rice, making it creamy and sweet with very little butter.

steps.t: Cut the pumpkin into 1 cm cubes and chop the onion. Keep the stock (store-bought is fine) hot over low heat.
Soften the onion in the oil over low heat for 5 minutes, until translucent.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Add the pumpkin and a ladle of stock. Cook for 10 minutes, until the cubes start to break down.
steps.label: Pumpkin

steps.t: Stir in the rice and toast it for 2 minutes, until the grains are glossy and hot.
steps.label: Toast rice

steps.t: Pour in the wine and let it evaporate, then add the stock one ladle at a time.

pressure.t: Pour in the wine and let it evaporate, then add 900 ml of hot stock all at once.

steps.t: Cook for 16–18 minutes, stirring often and adding stock as it dries, until the rice is al dente.
steps.label: Risotto

pressure.t: Lock the lid and cook for 7 minutes at pressure over low heat. Release the steam at once and stir.

steps.t: Turn off the heat, beat in the cold butter and Parmigiano, season with salt and pepper. Cover and rest 2 minutes.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Serve right away, loose and flowing on the plate. Finish with freshly ground pepper.

tips.t: Set aside a few roasted pumpkin cubes and scatter them on top when serving.
Sage crisped in butter or a pinch of nutmeg goes beautifully with the pumpkin.
Stir in a spoonful of gorgonzola instead of half the Parmigiano.

title: Risotto alla milanese
intro: Milan's golden risotto: saffron, beef stock and a generous finish of butter and cheese.

steps.t: Dissolve the saffron in a small ladle of hot stock. Keep the rest of the stock hot on the stove.
Finely chop the onion and soften it in half the butter with the marrow over low heat, until translucent.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Toast the rice for 2 minutes, stirring, until glossy, then add the wine and let it evaporate.
steps.label: Toast rice

steps.t: Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring often, and cook for 10 minutes.
steps.label: Risotto

steps.t: Pour in the saffron and cook for 7 more minutes, until the rice is al dente and still loose.
steps.label: Saffron

steps.t: Off the heat, beat in the remaining cold butter and the cheese vigorously. Taste for salt.
Cover and rest for 2 minutes, then spread it on flat plates, tapping the bottom so it settles.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: It is the classic partner for ossobuco: serve them together.
Add the saffron near the end: cooked too long it loses its aroma.
Next day, press it into a buttered pan and crisp both sides: that's risotto al salto.

title: Risi e bisi (rice and peas)
intro: Venice's spring dish: looser than a risotto and sweet with fresh peas.

steps.t: Slice the spring onion and soften it in the oil and half the butter over low heat, without browning.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Add the peas and a ladle of hot stock (store-bought is fine) and cook for 5 minutes, until tender.
steps.label: Peas

steps.t: Add the rice, stir it with the peas for 1 minute, then cover with two ladles of hot stock.

pressure.t: Add the rice, stir it with the peas for 1 minute, then pour in 1 litre of hot stock at once.

steps.t: Cook for 15–16 minutes, adding stock often: it should stay soupier than a risotto.
steps.label: Rice

pressure.t: Lock the lid and cook for 6 minutes at pressure. Release at once; loosen with a ladle of stock if thick.

steps.t: Turn off the heat and stir in the remaining butter, the Parmigiano and the parsley. Season.
Let it rest for 1 minute and serve in shallow bowls: a spoon works as well as a fork.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: With fresh peas, simmer the pods in the stock for 30 minutes: it tastes far more of peas.
Brown 60 g diced pancetta with the onion for the richer traditional version.

title: Paella valenciana
intro: Chicken, green beans and saffron, with a toasted crust on the bottom: the original paella.

ing.n: bone-in chicken thighs, cut into pieces

steps.t: Heat the oil in the paella pan, salt the chicken and brown it over medium heat until golden all over.
steps.label: Chicken

steps.t: Add the green beans, cut into pieces, and the cooked beans, and sauté them with the chicken for 3 minutes.
steps.label: Beans

steps.t: Clear the centre, cook the tomato for 3 minutes, then stir in the paprika for a few seconds without burning it.
steps.label: Tomato

steps.t: Pour in the water, add the saffron and salt, and simmer for 20 minutes to make the broth.
steps.label: Broth

steps.t: Taste: the broth should be slightly salty. Scatter the rice evenly and from now on don't stir.
Cook over high heat for 10 minutes, until the rice starts to show at the surface.
steps.label: High heat

steps.t: Lower the heat and cook for 9 more minutes, until the rice has absorbed all the liquid.
steps.label: Low heat

steps.t: Lay the rosemary on top and turn up the heat for 1 minute: the bottom should crackle and toast, not burn.
steps.label: Socarrat

steps.t: Take off the heat, cover with a clean tea towel and let it rest for 5 minutes before serving.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Use a wide, shallow pan: the rice should sit in a layer only 1–2 cm deep.
Serve with lemon wedges on the side and a crisp white wine or sangria.

title: Egg fried rice
intro: Day-old rice stir-fried over high heat: separate grains, soft egg and sweet peas.

ing.n: long-grain rice, cooked the day before and chilled

steps.t: Break up the cold rice with your hands. Finely dice the carrot, mince the garlic and slice the spring onions.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt. Heat 1 tbsp oil in the wok, scramble them softly and set aside.
Heat the remaining oil over high heat and stir-fry the garlic, carrot and white of the onions for 2 minutes.
steps.label: Veg

steps.t: Add the rice and peas and stir-fry for 4 minutes, pressing out lumps, until the grains are hot and jumping.
steps.label: Rice

steps.t: Pour the soy sauce around the edge of the wok, add the egg in pieces, the white pepper and the green onion.
Turn off the heat, drizzle with the sesame oil, toss once more and serve right away.

tips.t: Fresh rice turns mushy: with no leftovers, spread it on a tray and chill it for 1 hour.
Add 150 g prawns or diced cooked ham for a Yangzhou-style version.

title: Chicken biryani
intro: Marinated chicken and fragrant basmati rice, steamed together slowly under a sealed lid.

steps.t: Mix the chicken with yogurt, ginger, garlic, garam masala, chilli, turmeric, lemon and 1 tsp salt. Chill 1 hour.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: Meanwhile rinse the rice until the water runs clear and leave it to soak in cold water. Steep the saffron in the warm milk.
Thinly slice the onions and fry in the oil and half the ghee over medium heat until deep brown. Set half aside.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Add the chicken and its marinade to the remaining onions and cook over medium-high heat until the sauce thickens.
steps.label: Chicken

steps.t: Boil the drained rice in plenty of salted water with the whole spices for 5 minutes: still firm at the centre. Drain.
steps.label: Rice

steps.t: Spread the rice over the chicken. Scatter over mint, coriander, half the fried onions, the saffron milk and remaining ghee.
Seal the pot with foil and the lid and cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
steps.label: Dum

steps.t: Leave it closed for 5 minutes, then fold gently from the side and serve topped with the remaining crispy onions.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Serve with raita: yogurt, grated cucumber, mint and a pinch of cumin.
Don't rush the onions: the darker and crisper they are, the deeper the flavour.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge; reheat covered with a splash of water.

title: Mexican red rice
intro: Toasted rice cooked in blended tomato broth: the side dish at every Mexican table.

steps.t: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and drain it very well. Blend the tomatoes, onion and garlic until smooth.
Heat the oil and fry the rice over medium heat, stirring, for 7 minutes, until golden and nutty.
steps.label: Toast rice

steps.t: Pour in the tomato purée and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until it darkens and thickens.
steps.label: Tomato

steps.t: Add the hot stock (store-bought is fine), salt, carrot and peas, the chilli and coriander. Bring to the boil.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat for 18 minutes without lifting the lid, until the liquid is absorbed.
steps.label: Simmer

steps.t: Turn off the heat and rest, covered, for 10 minutes. Remove the coriander and chilli and fluff with a fork.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Toasting is everything: get the rice golden before the tomato and it stays fluffy.
Serve with black beans, tacos or grilled chicken, plus lime and sliced avocado.

title: Mujaddara
intro: Lentils and rice under a pile of caramelised onions: humble, filling and full of flavour.

steps.t: Rinse the lentils and simmer in 1 litre of water for 15 minutes, until tender but whole. Drain, keeping the water.
steps.label: Lentils

pressure.t: Rinse the lentils and pressure-cook them in 1 litre of water for 6 minutes at pressure. Drain, keeping the water.

steps.t: Meanwhile thinly slice the onions and cook in the oil over medium heat, stirring, until deep brown.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Lift out half the onions onto kitchen paper: they will crisp up as they cool.
In the same pot, toast the cumin and cinnamon for 30 seconds, then add the rinsed rice and stir for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, 450 ml of their cooking water and the salt. Bring to the boil.
Cover and cook over low heat for 18 minutes, until the rice is tender and the water absorbed.
steps.label: Simmer

steps.t: Rest, covered, for 10 minutes, fluff with a fork and serve heaped with the crispy onions.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Serve with a tomato, cucumber and lemon salad; add yogurt if you are not vegan.
It is just as good warm or cold, and keeps 3 days in the fridge.
